thread:
rajiv: Anyone run into HTTP/2 connections getting stuck after cancelling streaming requests? Using the Go client, we do an auth refresh + retry path and after a few cancels goroutine count creeps up and connections look like they're still occupied. Example from local repro:
```
goroutine 2155 [chan receive]:
net/http.(*persistConn).roundTrip(...)
internal/transport/stream.go:45: stream canceled
```
rajiv: Happens when ctx is canceled on the caller while the server is still sending chunks. The client retry then opens new streams but the old ones hang.

kate: Yep, seen this. Root causes we've hit: 1) not closing resp.Body on certain error paths, 2) creating new requests without correctly propagating the request ctx, and 3) http2 transport not noticing stream resets quickly.

kate: Quick checklist I use: always do `req = req.WithContext(ctx)` for every retry, and make sure to `defer func(){ if resp!=nil && resp.Body!=nil { resp.Body.Close() } }()` right after `client.Do`. Also prefer `io.Copy(io.Discard, resp.Body)` before Close for some servers.

lee: Also try configuring the http2 transport explicitly. We use the stdlib transport + `golang.org/x/net/http2`. Sample: `http2.ConfigureTransport(transport)` and set `transport.AllowHTTP=false`. For tuning: `IdleConnTimeout` on the base `http.Transport`, and `MaxConnsPerHost` helped in one case.

sam: FWIW I opened a small PR that adds an explicit stream reset on ctx cancel and an integration test that reproduces the leak: PR #1423. It wraps the RoundTripper so when ctx.Done() triggers we call CloseIdleConnections() as a last-resort for now. cc @kate for review.

rajiv: Nice. Does the wrapper reset break streaming semantics (we need to keep the stream open for async chunked responses)?

kate: It's a bit blunt and will drop streaming responses, so it's only safe for short-lived streams or when we do a reconnect/retry pattern. For genuine server-sent streams (long-lived), we need to ensure the server sends an explicit FIN and the client closes the body. If the server never closes, the stream will stay open until the transport decides to reclaim it.

lee: Another pragmatic workaround is to fall back to HTTP/1.1 for streaming endpoints that must support client-cancel semantics reliably: `transport.TLSNextProto = map[string]func(string, *tls.Conn) http.RoundTripper{}` will prevent automatic http2 upgrade. Not ideal but useful for a migration window.

rajiv: I'll try: 1) apply your PR locally, 2) ensure we propagate ctx on retry, 3) set `IdleConnTimeout=30s` + call `CloseIdleConnections()` after token refresh to avoid stuck streams. Will report back.

sam: Thanks — if your test reproduces it please paste logs here and I'll add a tighter fix (stream reset using http2 internals) instead of the CloseIdleConnections hack.

kate: If you open a follow-up issue, add a small perf/regression test. Also include the auth refresh sequence in the repro — that's a common trigger.

infra-bot: Reminder: eng-runtime canary deploy in 2h for the client patches :calendar:.

rajiv: Will do, thanks all. Ping me if you can review PR #1423 today, otherwise I'll land and follow up with a narrower fix if CI repros the leak. :thumbsup:
